title: CheckTest check report (schemaVersion 0.5)
description: Wire contract for a CheckTest `check` report at schemaVersion 0.5, describing the shape emitted by src/reporters/json.ts and the CLI no-adapter envelope in src/cli.ts. Stability policy (ADR-042, docs/product-contract.md section 3): 0.5 is additive only — nothing removed, renamed or reshaped; optional keys append after fixed keys; the version is bumped only when the report shape changes meaningfully, never per run. Consumers should check `schemaVersion` first and ignore unknown keys, so this schema accepts unknown keys at every level (additionalProperties: true). A normal check report has no `kind` key; the JSON-only no-adapter envelope is the $defs.noAdapterEnvelope variant. This file is descriptive, not generative: the reporter remains the single producer.

test.description: Identity of the analyzed file. Per-test identities live in testResults[].test.

analysisStatus.description: Whether the collector could analyze the input at all. An UNSUPPORTED analysis is still a completed analysis: it is reported here, not as a verdict, and keeps exit 0 when any scope reached a verdict.

evaluationStatus.description: Whether the rule engine reached a verdict across the evaluation scopes. FAILED means NO verdict was produced (the rule was never evaluated: an aborted scope, or zero scopes). It is not a rule FAIL and not an analysis failure.

completeness.description: Evidence completeness at file scope, independent of analysisStatus and of any verdict.

scope.description: The analysis construct the collector scanned (e.g. 'test-body'). This is not the subject identity: attribution is structural, through the file-level `evidence` map versus each testResults[].evidence map.

test_type.description: The declared or classified test type plus how it was decided. An inferred classification is never authoritative.

capabilities.description: Named collector capability statuses the caller could rely on. Keys are adapter-defined capability ids.

evidence.description: File-level aggregate evidence, keyed by evidence type id. The map key names the evidence type, so the record never repeats it. A per-declaration evidence map appears in testResults[].evidence; the two levels are the structural attribution boundary.

ruleResults.description: The flattened, authoritative findings list in scope order — one list, with no separate file-level aggregate verdict beside it. An aborted scope contributes no entry (never a synthetic verdict).

schemaVersion.description: Wire-contract version. 0.5 adds the OPTIONAL adapter/decidedBy envelope fields and the JSON-only no-adapter envelope, all additive: nothing removed or renamed. Bumped only when the report shape changes meaningfully, never per run.

kind.description: Present ONLY on the no-adapter envelope variant (value 'check'); a normal check report omits it, following the doctor/explain machine-payload convention.

adapter.description: Id of the adapter that produced the analysis. Optional and present-only; absent means the envelope predates adapter identity or no adapter ran.

decidedBy.description: Which dispatch layer selected the adapter. Optional and present-only; only meaningful together with `adapter`. 'unsupported' never reaches the report because it takes the no-adapter envelope path.

deprecatedSince.description: Version in which the evaluated rule was deprecated. Present ONLY when the rule declares one; omitted, never an empty string.

reasonCode.description: Machine-readable reason for a non-report outcome. Present ONLY on the no-adapter envelope ('NO_ADAPTER_MATCHED'); normal reports omit it.

reason.description: Human-readable explanation. Present on the no-adapter envelope; normal findings carry their own per-verdict `reason`.

testResults.description: One record per test declaration the engine evaluated, in declaration order. Empty when no declaration was evaluated (including a file that supplied zero tests); a subject-level fallback verdict is never copied onto a declaration.

summary.description: Verdict counts across evaluation scopes. `failed` counts scopes that did NOT end in a clean PASS: a FAIL verdict PLUS a scope the engine aborted (evaluationStatus FAILED), which has no verdict and appears in no per-result counter. Consequently total need not equal pass + fail + indeterminate + not_applicable when aborted scopes exist.

testType.description: Test type. UNKNOWN is the default and is never silently inferred as one of the other values.

classificationSource.description: How test_type.value was decided. INFERRED is never authoritative.

testSubject.description: Identity of the analyzed file. `framework` and `type` are present only when the collector knew them.

analysisStatus.description: Collector status: SUCCESS = required steps ran and returned interpretable output; UNSUPPORTED = source, language, framework or capability outside supported scope; FAILED = a required step failed or its output could not be interpreted.

evaluationStatus.description: Engine reach: EVALUATED = the rule was decided and a finding exists; FAILED = a required analysis step failed and the rule was never asked, so no RuleResult exists and none is invented. FAILED is never a verdict, never a rule FAIL, and never laundered into INDETERMINATE. Across several scopes, EVALUATED wins if ANY scope produced a verdict.

completeness.description: Evidence completeness. Separate from analysisStatus and from verdicts; NOT_APPLICABLE is used only where explicitly justified.

provenance.description: Where an evidence value came from. This is not a confidence score.

availability.description: Whether the collector could decide the value at all. Independent of provenance and of evidenceStrength; the three axes never substitute for one another.

collectionStatus.description: Collection coverage for one evidence type: COMPLETE = the scan ran to completion; PARTIAL = some forms were unscannable; UNAVAILABLE = the collector could not scan.

evidenceStrength.description: How an assertion was established along the syntax-to-execution axis. Never a substitute for availability: a strength never turns UNKNOWN into KNOWN, and an omitted strength must not be read as EXECUTION_ESTABLISHED.

ruleResult.description: The rule's verdict. N/A means the rule does not apply to this subject; INDETERMINATE means it applies but evidence is insufficient, incomplete or conflicting.

ruleStatus.description: Lifecycle status of the rule that produced the finding. Required: a finding is one rule's verdict, so its lifecycle state is part of that verdict's identity.

location.description: A source position the collector can point at. Never fabricated: the key is absent when no position is known.

column.description: Present only when known; never a fabricated or null column.

evidenceConflict.description: A second, disagreeing value for the same evidence type. Both values and their provenance are preserved; a conflict does not by itself imply incompleteness — the rule applies its conflicting-evidence policy.

value.description: The conflicting value. null when the provider reported none (JSON has no undefined).

countReasons.description: Count plus the reasons for it, attached to a per-declaration evidence record. Present-only: the producing field itself is omitted when the adapter has nothing to report.

evidenceRecord.description: One normalized evidence item. `type` is deliberately absent: the map key this record sits under already names it, and repeating it would be the only field needing a rename. `scope` names the analysis construct scanned, not the subject: it never says WHICH test or file the value belongs to. Attribution is structural (file-level evidence map vs per-declaration testResults[].evidence). The mutation_score record is file-level by design and must NEVER be read as individual-test attribution.

value.description: The evidence value. null (not absent) when the producer had no value, so the field set never depends on what the collector knew.

scope.description: The analysis construct scanned (e.g. 'test-body'). Not the subject identity.

reason.description: Required whenever the value is unknown, partial or unavailable. Present-only otherwise.

conflicts.description: Present only when populated: an empty array carries no information, so the producer drops it. A populated array preserves both disagreeing values with their provenance.

provider.description: Provider identity. Present-only and only meaningful when provenance is EXTERNAL.

provider_version.description: Provider/tool version. Present-only and only meaningful when provenance is EXTERNAL.

source_revision.description: Source revision the external evidence was derived from. Present-only and only meaningful when provenance is EXTERNAL.

unestablished_assertions.description: Per-declaration unestablished-assertion signal. Present-only on per-declaration records; file-level aggregate records leave it unset.

unclassified_constructs.description: Per-declaration unclassified-construct signal. Present-only on per-declaration records.

property_based.description: Present-only when the producer detected property-based (@given) cases. Detection-affirmative only; a count is not case-exhaustive.

evidenceStrength.description: HOW the evidence was established. Present-only; omitted when the producer classifies no strength.

finding.description: One rule's verdict for one scope. `reason` is always present — no silent verdicts. Optional metadata is copied from the evaluated rule, never re-authored, and omitted (not empty) when the rule declares none.

reason.description: Why this verdict was reached. Always present.

evidence.description: Evidence TYPE ids the rule consulted, in evaluation order — not evidence records. The records live in the envelope or per-test evidence map.

description.description: The rule's own description, copied from its metadata. Present-only.

rationale.description: Why the rule exists, copied from its metadata. Present-only.

limitations.description: What the verdict does NOT establish, copied from the rule's metadata. Present-only.

docsUrl.description: Reference into the rule's own definition. Present-only.

evidenceStrength.description: Strength of the evidence the verdict rests on, copied from the referenced evidence record. Present-only; never a certainty score.

provenance.description: Provenance derived from the evidence record the finding references. Absent when no such record exists — never fabricated.

availability.description: Availability derived from the evidence record the finding references. Absent when no such record exists — never fabricated.

test_id.description: Test identity of the per-test scope this finding belongs to. Present ONLY for a per-test scope: a subject-level finding (including the file-level mutation finding) omits it, and that absence is the non-attribution marker. Never implies test attribution when absent.

completeness.description: Completeness of the scope the finding was decided in. Present-only.

testIdentity.description: Identity of one test declaration site. The id is deterministic: <file>#<declaration>@<line>:<index>, with no clock or randomness.

line.description: 1-based source line of the declaration call.

framework.description: Per-declaration framework. Present-only: the TypeScript adapter carries none.

testResult.description: One declaration's slice of the report: its own identity, analysis status, evidence and findings. Nothing here is derived from a sibling, so a per-test FAIL cannot be masked by a file-level PASS and a file-level FAIL cannot be attributed to a test that did not earn it.

evidence.description: This declaration's evidence only, keyed by evidence type id. References never reach a sibling declaration.

ruleResults.description: This scope's findings: zero when the scope was aborted, never a stand-in verdict.

deprecatedSince.description: Version in which the evaluated rule was deprecated. Present-only.

fail.description: Scopes whose rule verdict is FAIL. Does not include aborted scopes.

failed.description: Scopes that did NOT end in a clean PASS: FAIL verdicts PLUS scopes the engine aborted (evaluationStatus FAILED), which produced no verdict. Dual meaning is DOCUMENTED here only; no additional wire key disambiguates it at 0.5.

noAdapterSummary.description: The zeroed summary of the no-adapter envelope: absence of analysis is explicit, never a PASS or FAIL.

noAdapterEnvelope.description: The JSON-only no-verdict envelope emitted on stdout when no adapter matches the test file (default JSON format). It is a no-verdict statement, not an error object and not a rule report: schemaVersion stays 0.5 (ADR-042) and the SARIF path is deliberately unchanged (stderr prose, empty stdout, exit 2). evaluationStatus FAILED here means no analysis ran, so no verdict was produced.

reason.description: Human-readable diagnostic naming the file, suggesting `checktest doctor --test <path>` and `--adapter <id>`.

test.description: Subject identity is limited to the file because no adapter ran.

ruleResults.description: Always empty in the shipped 0.5 envelope: no rule was evaluated, and no verdict is invented.

testResults.description: Always empty in the shipped 0.5 envelope.
